questions: Where do you live? What do you like about it?
Do you prefer living in a flat or a house? Why?
What would you change about your neighbourhood?
What do you usually do at the weekend?
Tell me about a hobby you have.
What did you do last weekend?
What are you studying? Why did you choose it?
What would your ideal job be?
How do you usually prepare for exams?
Where did you go on your last holiday?
What kind of holiday do you prefer? Why?
Which country would you like to visit in the future?
How often do you use your phone during the day? What for?
Which piece of technology could you not live without?
Tell me about a time when technology did not work as you expected.
What do you do to stay healthy?
Do you enjoy playing or watching sport? Why?
How much sleep do you usually get, and does it affect your day?
What is your favourite meal, and who usually cooks it?
Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants? Why?
Is there any food you tried recently that surprised you?
What kind of films or series do you enjoy watching?
How do you usually find out about the news?
Have you read a book or watched a programme recently that you would recommend?
Do you enjoy shopping? Why or why not?
How has the way you shop changed in the last few years?
What was the last thing you bought that you were really pleased with?
Who do you spend most of your free time with?
How often do you see your relatives, and what do you do together?
What qualities do you value most in a good friend?

cards.a: A family having a picnic in a park
cards.b: A group of friends eating in a restaurant
cards.question: Why might the people have chosen to eat in these places?

cards.a: A student studying alone in a library
cards.b: Students working together on a project in a classroom
cards.question: How might the students be feeling?

cards.a: A person running along a beach at sunrise
cards.b: A group of people playing basketball in a gym
cards.question: What are the advantages of exercising in these ways?

cards.a: A tourist taking photos in front of a famous monument
cards.b: A tourist relaxing in a hotel pool
cards.question: Why might people choose these kinds of holiday?

cards.a: A chef cooking in a busy restaurant kitchen
cards.b: A person cooking dinner at home for their family
cards.question: What might be difficult about these situations?

cards.a: A person working at a laptop in a café
cards.b: A person working in a crowded open-plan office
cards.question: Which might be better for concentrating, and why?

cards.a: A man waiting for a crowded bus in the rain
cards.b: A woman cycling to work along a quiet road
cards.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of travelling in these ways?

cards.a: A customer buying fresh vegetables at an outdoor market
cards.b: A person ordering clothes on a laptop at home
cards.question: Why might people prefer to shop in these ways?

cards.a: A couple watching a film in a busy cinema
cards.b: A person watching a series on a tablet in bed
cards.question: Why might the people have chosen to watch something in these ways?

cards.a: A family in a small flat in the middle of a big city
cards.b: A family in a house with a garden in a village
cards.question: What might be the advantages and disadvantages of living in these places?

cards.a: Volunteers cleaning rubbish from a beach
cards.b: Children planting trees in a town park
cards.question: Why do you think these people decided to take part in these activities?

cards.a: A teenager playing a video game alone in his room
cards.b: A group of friends playing a board game around a table
cards.question: What might the people enjoy about these activities?

cards.a: A crowd watching a famous singer in a huge stadium
cards.b: A small band playing for a few people in a local pub
cards.question: Which experience might be more memorable, and why?

cards.b: A large family celebrating a birthday around a table

tasks.central: A school is planning to organise an event to raise money for charity. Talk about how good each of these ideas would be, then decide which would raise the most money.
tasks.decision: Which would raise the most money?

tasks.central: A town wants to encourage young people to spend more time outdoors. Talk about the advantages of each idea and decide which is the best.
tasks.decision: Which is the best idea for the town?

tasks.central: Some students want to improve their English over the summer. Talk about how useful each way would be, then decide which is the most effective.
tasks.decision: Which is the most effective way?

tasks.central: A city council wants to reduce the amount of traffic in the town centre. Talk about how effective each of these ideas would be, then decide which one the council should choose first.
options: free car parks outside the centre
tasks.decision: Which idea should the council choose first?

tasks.central: A school wants to encourage students to lead a healthier lifestyle. Talk about how useful each of these ideas would be, then decide which would have the biggest effect.
options: a later start to the school day
tasks.decision: Which idea would have the biggest effect?

tasks.central: A youth club is losing members and wants to attract more teenagers. Talk about how attractive each of these activities would be for young people, then decide which would attract the most teenagers.
options: a trip to a theme park
tasks.decision: Which activity would attract the most teenagers?

tasks.central: A school wants to reduce the amount of plastic waste it produces. Talk about how helpful each of these ideas would be, then decide which should be introduced first.
options: a ban on plastic bottles in the café
tasks.decision: Which idea should be introduced first?

tasks.central: A town wants to make a visit more enjoyable for foreign tourists. Talk about how good each of these ideas would be, then decide which would help visitors most.
options: a cheap day pass for museums
tasks.decision: Which idea would help visitors the most?

tasks.central: A school wants to help new students feel welcome in their first month. Talk about how useful each of these ideas would be, then decide which is the most important.
options: a buddy system with older students
a school guide with a map
a meeting with a class tutor
tasks.decision: Which idea is the most important for new students?

tasks.central: A company wants its employees to feel happier and less stressed at work. Talk about how effective each of these ideas would be, then decide which would make the biggest difference to employees.
tasks.decision: Which would make the biggest difference to employees?
